Header: Barley yellow dwarf viruses Barley yellow dwarf (BYD)

Prevention: Barley yellow dwarf virus is transmitted from plant to plant by different species of aphids
Select small grain cultivars eg kenya sunbird, kenya hawk 12, with documented resistance or tolerance to the virus from certified dealers, i.e. simlaws
Plough deeply affected post harvested areas to ensure complete decomposition of all plant material
Practice crop rotation with non host plants such as green grams, kales and spinach
Proper spacing of the plants at 80-120 plants/square metre apart to optimize aeration
Early planting to avoid aphid population build up
Monitoring: Look out for small pale green insect (aphids) with an elongated, spindle- shaped body under the leaf one week after crop emergence
Check for chlorotic to reddened leaves in young plants.
Upright stiff leaves with serrated edges, stunted plants
Take action when 50% of cereal tillers have 15 or more aphids three weeks after emergence
Direct Control: Remove and destroy affected plant parts by burying them 1m deeply in the ground or burning
Destroy and remove volunteer cereals to help reduce or delay pest build-up
Add a layer of organic manure mixed deeper into the soil up to 20 cm at a rate of (2 tones/ acre) and irrigate the farm to prevent water stress to the plants
Restrictions: When using a pesticide, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label
Do not use chemicals with the same mode of action year after year as this can lead to resistance
Always consult the most recent list of registered pesticides (PCPB)
